cards.title: One engine state union: every non-ready engine state carries its move

cards.body:
## Summary
The engine's standing is a product of eight inputs (probes, checking, problem, loaded, stored engine, daemon engine, health, error) decided by four parallel if-chains - selectSetup's startFailure, pendingEngineOf, engineFact and notReadyBecause - each checking a different subset in a different order. Two of the combinations they miss are dead ends a person reaches in ordinary use. Fold the chains into one discriminated union, engineStateOf(model), whose every state names its move, and make the four exports projections of it.

## Description
The dead end: after the letter, a person chooses Codex in Mind (row written, restart notice shown) and does not restart; the Claude Code daemon then fails or stops. startFailure requires the daemon to be on the stored engine (model.ts:182), the restart notice requires health 'ready' (model.ts:240), and engineFact's mismatch branch runs before any health check (readiness.ts:66), so the screen says 'Codex is chosen, but Athena is still running on Claude Code' over a dead daemon, and offers no button: pressing Codex again only rewrites the row (settings.ts:209). A second gap: an empty daemonEngine with a failed health reads 'still starting up on it' (readiness.ts:73) - a failure dressed as a wait, which the failure-states technique names as the class to close.

engine-state.ts exports `type EngineState = {kind:'unchecked'|'checking'|'check-failed'|'not-installed'|'signed-out'|'other-chosen'|'awaiting-daemon'|'starting'|'pending-switch'|'down-on-other'|'failed'|'stopped'|'running', engine, running, move:'check'|'restart'|'choose'|'sign-in'|'install'|'wait'|null}` and the pure `engineStateOf(source)`. selectSetup computes it once; startFailure, pendingEngine, engineFact, notReadyBecause and restartNotice read it. The words stay in readiness.ts. The exhaustive 960-row table test pins the invariant that makes this a class fix rather than two patches: no non-ready state without a move, no 'running' or 'starting' sentence over a failed or stopped daemon.

This is the async-ui-states failure-states rule (a failure is distinct from a wait, and carries the action that fixes it) and its state-model rule (derive UI states from the machinery once). It does not touch r1's display-authority card (Standing -> word/tone in scenes); it is the layer under it.

## Flow
- before: Codex chosen, Claude Code daemon fails -> Mind engine: 'still running on Claude Code', no ProblemNote, no restart notice -> the person must quit the app (the launch reads the store, ADR 0085) to recover
- after: the same -> 'Athena stopped on Claude Code.' with the daemon's reason and 'Start on Codex' -> one press, actions.restart on the stored engine

## Expected impact
A whole class (non-ready engine states with no action, failures phrased as waits) closes and is pinned by a table, and the next engine-state bug is a missing row in one union rather than a fifth chain. The fix reaches both surfaces (first act, Mind) with no scene edit, because they already draw startFailure.

## Evaluation
Claim: every non-ready engine state carries a move, and no failed daemon reads as running or starting
Before: 0 of 4 behaviour cases pass (cases 0-3); the 960-row table finds the down-on-other and empty-engine-failed rows moveless
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases (vitest, offline)
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence: model.ts:180-183: `(source.daemonLoaded ?? true) && daemonEngine === source.engine && (health === "failed" || health === "stopped")`. model.ts:240: `if (health !== "ready" || !running) return null;`. readiness.ts:66-75: `if (model.daemonEngine !== model.engine) { ... summary: model.daemonEngine ? `${label} is chosen, but Athena is still running on ${engineLabel(model.daemonEngine)}` : `${label} is chosen, and Athena is still starting up on it` }` - no health read before it. settings.ts:209: `return settings.onboarded ? settings.setEngine(engine) : chooseFirstRunEngine(engine);`. model.test.ts:134 pins `selectSetup(sources({ daemonHealth: "failed", daemonEngine: "codex" })).startFailure).toBeNull()`. Consumers of startFailure: EngineSection.tsx:75 (ProblemNote, onRetry=actions.restart), mind/view.tsx:156, mind/shared.tsx:66.

cards.title: The microphone's answer is known on arrival, follows the OS switch, says how to undo

acceptance: mic.ts readMicPermission(fake permissions whose query({name:'microphone'}) resolves {state:'denied'}) -> {standing:'denied', recalled:true}; 'granted' -> {standing:'granted', recalled:true}; 'prompt' -> {standing:'unknown', recalled:false}; a query that throws or permissions undefined -> {standing:'unknown', recalled:false} (no prompt is ever raised by reading)

cards.body:
## Summary
A person who refused the microphone once is told 'not asked yet' on every later visit, and pressing Check again re-fails instantly with 'NotAllowedError: Permission denied...'. The platform already remembers the answer; read it on arrival (no prompt), follow it live, and say in plain words how to give it back.

## Description
mic.ts adds readMicPermission(permissions) over navigator.permissions.query({name:'microphone'}) - a read that never prompts - and watchMicPermission(status, onChange) over the status's change event. useSetupModel seeds the mic standing from it on mount and subscribes for the hook's life, so turning the OS switch on while the Mind depth is open flips the row to granted without a press. micRemedy(standing, platform) turns a denial into the platform's re-grant path (Windows: Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone, desktop apps allowed); micFact's denied summary becomes that sentence and micDetail keeps the browser's own words after it. Where the Permissions API is missing or throws, nothing changes: the standing stays unknown and Check the microphone works as today.

This is the voice-io stt-pipeline rule (denial is a designed state, remembered, with platform-specific recovery) and closes the deviation already recorded against setup/index.ts. Nothing is stored and no data leaves the device.

## Flow
- before: refuse once -> next visit Mind Microphone reads 'not asked yet' -> press Check -> raw NotAllowedError -> the person searches for why push-to-talk is off
- after: next visit reads 'refused' with 'Turn it on in Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone' -> the person flips it -> the row turns granted on its own

## Expected impact
The one optional capability in setup stops lying about its own history and stops being a loop with no exit. Both the first act's Voice step and the Mind Microphone level read it with no scene change.

## Evaluation
Claim: a remembered denial is shown on arrival with its remedy, and a re-grant is seen without a press
Before: 0 of 6 behaviour cases pass (cases 0-5)
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases (vitest + jsdom, fake Permissions API, offline)
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence: index.ts:55-58: `const [mic, setMic] = useState<{ standing: MicStanding; detail: string }>({ standing: "unknown", detail: "" });` - no read on mount. readiness.ts:152-158: `case "denied": return { ...base, standing: "missing", summary: model.micDetail || "refused by the webview" }; ... default: return { ...base, standing: "unknown", summary: "not asked yet" };`. lib/voice.ts:366-383: the standing comes only from a getUserMedia call. grep -rn permissions over apps/desktop/src/lib, stores, modules/voice: no navigator.permissions read anywhere. registry-map voice-io state 'deviation', evidence 'apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/index.ts:53 The microphone answer is hook-local state seeded unknown, so a denial is forgotten on the next visit...'.
